definition_zh: 安静的；平静的；僻静的；低调的；安宁；使安静
definition_en: making little or no noise; calm and not excited; with little activity or few people; not attracting attention; a state of calm; to make someone or something quiet
core_image: 清晨空荡的阅览室，只有窗外一线光落在桌面上
scene: 清晨的图书馆里，只有翻书声和远处钟摆的滴答，管理员把脚步放得很轻。The reading room was so quiet that a dropped pen sounded like a knock.
sceneCN: 这里 quiet 是「安静、几乎没有声音」（第 1 个义项：声音很小的状态）；句意为阅览室安静得连掉一支笔都像敲门。画面里可留意：翻开的书、远处的钟、轻放的脚步。

pos.zh: 安静的；平静的；僻静的；低调的

derivatives.zh: quiet 加 -ly，指安静地、不动声色地
quiet 加 -ness，指安静、平静的状态
quiet 加 -en，英式用法，指使安静下来
与 quiet 同族的书面词，指宁静、安详的心境

senses.title: Making little or no noise
senses.definition: making very little sound, so that small noises become noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 几乎不发出声音，以至于细小的响动都变得明显
senses.example: The library was so quiet that I could hear the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆安静得我能听见钟的走时声。
senses.why: Latin quietus meant at rest, and a place at rest is first of all a place without noise.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quietus 意为处于休息状态，而一个休息中的地方首先就是没有声音的地方。

senses.title: Calm and not excited
senses.definition: showing no strong feeling, worry or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 不显露强烈情绪、担忧或兴奋的
senses.example: She stayed quiet while the others argued around her.
senses.exampleCN: 旁人在她周围争吵时，她保持平静。
senses.why: Rest of body and rest of mind were one idea in Latin, so the word also names a person whose feelings are still.
senses.whyCN: 在拉丁语里，身体的休息与心境的休息是同一个概念，因此这个词也指情绪静止不动的人。

senses.title: With little activity or few people
senses.definition: having little traffic, activity or company
senses.definitionCN: 车流、活动或人都不多的
senses.example: They spent the weekend in a quiet village near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边一个僻静的村子过了周末。
senses.why: A place can be at rest as a whole, not only silent in sound, so the word also describes a district with little going on.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方可以整体处于休息状态，不只是声音小，所以这个词也形容缺少活动的地区。

senses.title: Not attracting attention
senses.definition: modest and deliberately kept out of public view
senses.definitionCN: 谦逊并且刻意不引人注意的
senses.example: He led a quiet life and rarely spoke in public.
senses.exampleCN: 他过着低调的生活，很少在公开场合发言。
senses.why: Someone who does not make noise is also someone who does not make a public fuss, so quiet came to mean unassuming.
senses.whyCN: 不制造声音的人，也是不公开张扬的人，于是 quiet 引申为不摆架子、不引人注目。

senses.title: A state of calm and silence
senses.definition: a period or condition of calm, silence and freedom from disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 一段平静、安静且不被打扰的时光或状态
senses.example: We enjoyed the quiet of the early morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们享受清晨的宁静。
senses.why: The adjective was turned into a noun, naming the state itself rather than the thing that has it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词被转化为名词，指这种状态本身，而不是具有这种状态的事物。

senses.title: To make quiet
senses.definition: to cause a person, animal or place to become calm or silent
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人、动物或场所变得平静或无声
senses.example: The teacher quieted the class with a single look.
senses.exampleCN: 老师只看了一眼就让全班安静下来。
senses.why: Once quiet was both a state and a quality, English formed a verb meaning to bring that state about.
senses.whyCN: quiet 既是状态又是性质，英语便由此造出动词，意为使这种状态出现。

intro.en: Quiet comes from the Latin word for rest, passed through French; rest of body, of mind and of a place all lie inside the same root.
intro.cn: quiet 源自拉丁语表示休息的词，经法语传来；身体、心境与地方的休息都装在同一词根里。

items.en: Quies meant rest, repose and freedom from activity, the opposite of motion and disturbance.
items.cn: quies 意为休息、安歇、不活动，与运动和打扰相对。

items.en: Quietus was the adjective and noun of that rest, describing someone or something at peace.
items.cn: quietus 是表示这种休息的形容词与名词，形容处于安宁中的人或物。

items.en: Old French quite carried the sense of calm and free from disturbance into the language of England.
items.cn: 古法语 quite 把平静、不受打扰的意思带进了英格兰的语言。

items.en: Middle English quiet described both a silent place and a calm mind, and later gained the sense of modest.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quiet 既形容寂静的地方，也形容平静的心，后来又获得「低调」义。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for sound, for calm, for lonely places, for modest lives and for the state itself.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指声音、平静、僻静之处、低调生活以及状态本身。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same root and one word that merely looks close; the near-meaning group gathers words for silence and calm.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的形式，以及一个只是长得像的词；近义组收表示寂静与平静的词。

entries.definition: To stop or leave, a different word that happens to share the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 停止或离开，与 quiet 同源但词义已分家的另一个词。

entries.definition: Not moving and not making noise.

entries.definitionCN: 不受打扰或没有冲突的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as rest: a body at rest is still, a room at rest is silent, and a life at rest is modest.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「休息」开始：休息的身体是静止的，休息的房间是安静的，休息的人生是低调的。

normal.en: Quiet and quit come from the same Latin word for rest, but quit took the road of leaving while quiet stayed with silence.
normal.cn: quiet 与 quit 同出拉丁语「休息」一词，但 quit 走上了「离开」的路，quiet 留在「安静」这边。

normal.en: Quieten is the British verb, while American speakers more often use quiet down.
normal.cn: quieten 是英式动词，美式更常用 quiet down。

normal.en: Peace and quiet puts two nouns together, because peace of mind and silence of place are close companions.
normal.cn: peace and quiet 把两个名词并在一起，因为心的安宁与周围安静常常相伴。

normal.en: Quietly is the adverb: it tells how a door was closed or how a person accepted news.
normal.cn: quietly 是副词：它说明门是怎样关上的，或一个人怎样接受了消息。

normal.en: A quiet street has few cars, while a quiet voice has low volume; the same word covers both kinds of little.
normal.cn: quiet street 车少，quiet voice 声小；同一个词涵盖了两种「少」。

abstract.en: Quiet is not the absence of life but the absence of disturbance, which is why a busy mind can still live a quiet life.
abstract.cn: 安静不是没有生命，而是没有打扰，所以忙碌的头脑仍可过安静的生活。

abstract.en: A quiet person often holds more than a loud one says, and the word quietly carries both praise and suspicion.
abstract.cn: 安静的人往往比喧哗的人说得少而想得多，而 quietly 这个词既带着赞许，也带着疑虑。

abstract.en: Every room has a quiet of its own, and people recognize it before they can name it.
abstract.cn: 每个房间都有自己的安静，人们先认出它，才说得出它。

examples.en: Please keep quiet while the baby is asleep.
examples.cn: 孩子睡觉时请保持安静。

examples.en: The street is quiet in the morning but busy after five.
examples.cn: 这条街早晨很僻静，五点以后就忙了。

examples.en: She quieted the dog with a soft word.
examples.cn: 她轻声一句话就让狗安静下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快饿特」——饿到没力气说话，全场安安静静，记住 quiet 是安静的。

root: 拉丁语 quies（休息）→ quietus（安宁的）→ 古法语 quite → 英语 quiet；同族有 quietly、quieten、quietude，以及词义分家的 quit。

sensesIntro.en: The core is rest; the senses divide into silence of sound, calm of feeling, emptiness of place, modesty of life, the state itself and the act of causing it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是休息；义项分为声音的寂静、情绪的平静、地方的冷清、生活的低调、状态本身，以及使这种状态出现的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty reading room at dawn, one stripe of light on a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明时空荡的阅览室，一线光落在桌面上。

branches.en: a pen falling in a silent room
branches.cn: 寂静房间里落下的一支笔

branches.en: hands folded while others argue
branches.cn: 别人争吵时交叠的双手

branches.en: a lane with one lit window
branches.cn: 只有一扇窗亮着的小巷

branches.en: a man who never takes the front seat
the same rest, once enjoyed and once imposed
branches.cn: 同一种休息，一次被享受，一次被施加

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin noun for rest and its adjective, with English endings that build adverbs, nouns and a verb of calming.
intro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁语表示休息的名词及其形容词，加上构成副词、名词与「使安静」动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around quies is small but it reaches English through more than one French route.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 quies 的拉丁词群不大，却经由不止一条法语路径进入英语。

definition_zh: 安静地；轻声地；平静地；不张扬地
definition_en: with little or no noise; in a calm way, without fuss; without attracting public attention
core_image: 一双把门轻轻带上的手，门把转得极慢
scene: 病房里，护士把门轻轻带上，连门把都转得很慢，怕吵醒刚睡着的人。She quietly closed the door so the patient could sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 quietly 是「安静地、轻声地」（第 1 个义项：几乎不发出声音地做某事）；句意为她轻轻关上门，好让病人能睡。画面里可留意：缓慢转动的门把、病房的走廊灯。

pos.zh: 安静地；轻声地；平静地；不张扬地

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的形容词，指安静的、平静的
quiet 加 -ness，指安静的状态
quiet 加 -en，指使安静下来

senses.title: With little or no noise
senses.definition: making very little sound while doing something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事时几乎不发出声音
senses.example: She closed the door quietly behind her.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻把门在身后关上。
senses.why: The adverb adds the manner ending to the adjective of silence, so it describes an action carried out without noise.
senses.whyCN: 副词在表示寂静的形容词后加上方式词尾，因此描述一个不带声音完成的动作。

senses.title: In a calm way
senses.definition: without showing strong feeling or making a fuss
senses.definitionCN: 不显露强烈情绪、不吵不闹地
senses.example: He quietly accepted the criticism and went back to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静地接受了批评，回去继续工作。
senses.why: Calm of feeling was part of the adjective's meaning, and the adverb carries that stillness into the description of an action.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的平静本就是形容词含义的一部分，副词把这种静止带进了对动作的描述。

senses.title: Without attracting attention
senses.definition: in a way that avoids public notice
senses.definitionCN: 避免引起公众注意地
senses.example: The company quietly expanded while its rivals argued in public.
senses.exampleCN: 对手公开争吵时，这家公司悄然扩张。
senses.why: A person who makes no noise attracts no notice, so the adverb came to describe action done out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 不制造声音的人也不引起注意，于是这个副词转而描述在人们视线之外完成的行动。

intro.en: Quietly is the adjective quiet plus the English adverb ending -ly; its history is the history of quiet.
intro.cn: quietly 是形容词 quiet 加英语副词词尾 -ly；它的历史就是 quiet 的历史。

items.en: The root meant rest, and rest of body, mind and place is the source of every sense.
items.cn: 词根意为休息，身体、心境与地方的休息是一切义项的源头。

items.en: The adjective described someone or something at peace, and English took it through French.
items.cn: 这个形容词形容处于安宁中的人或物，英语经法语把它接受过来。

items.en: Middle English quiet already covered silence, calm and modesty, so the adverb inherited all three.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quiet 已涵盖寂静、平静与低调，副词便继承了这三层意思。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb of manner, telling how an action is done.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成方式副词，说明一个动作是怎样做的。

items.en: Modern English uses quietly for sound, for calm behaviour and for action kept out of public view.
items.cn: 现代英语用 quietly 指声音、举止的平静，以及避开公众视线的行动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base adjective and its relatives; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of softness and calm.
note.cn: 形近组收基础形容词及其亲属；近义组收表示轻声与平静的副词。

entries.definition: Making little noise or showing little excitement.
entries.definitionCN: 声音小或不显露兴奋的。

entries.definition: Without making any sound at all.
In a way that avoids attracting notice.

normalIntro.en: The word simply says that an action was done in the manner of quiet: little sound, little fuss, little notice.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只是说，一个动作是以 quiet 的方式完成的：声音少、动静少、惹人注意少。

normal.en: Quietly is quiet plus -ly; if you know the adjective, you already know the adverb.
normal.cn: quietly 就是 quiet 加 -ly；认识形容词，也就认识了这个副词。

normal.en: More quietly and most quietly are the comparatives, because a long adverb prefers more to -er.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more quietly 与 most quietly，因为较长的副词更爱用 more 而不用 -er。

normal.en: Speak quietly is the standard phrase for lowering your voice in a shared room.
normal.cn: speak quietly 是在公共房间里压低声音的标准说法。

normal.en: Quietly confident describes someone sure of themselves without needing to show it.
normal.cn: quietly confident 形容一个人自信却不必表现出来。

normal.en: A thing done quietly is often done well, because it was done without a performance.
normal.cn: 安静做成的事往往做得好，因为它没有被表演化。

abstract.en: The adverb quietly hides its subject: we often hear the result and never the person who acted.
abstract.cn: 副词 quietly 把动作的主语藏了起来：我们常听到结果，却从不知道是谁做的。

abstract.en: Doing something quietly can be a form of respect, and also a form of power.
abstract.cn: 安静地做一件事，既可能是一种尊重，也可能是一种权力。

abstract.en: A culture that praises speaking loudly will still depend on those who work quietly.
abstract.cn: 一个赞美大声表达的文化，仍然依赖那些安静做事的人。

examples.en: He quietly shut the gate so the dog would not bark.
examples.cn: 他悄悄关上院门，免得狗叫起来。

examples.en: She quietly explained the mistake without blaming anyone.
examples.cn: 她平静地解释了这个错误，没有责怪任何人。

examples.en: The village quietly became a favourite place for painters.
examples.cn: 这个村子悄然成了画家们偏爱的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快饿特利」——饿得说话都没力气，只能安安静静，记住 quietly 是安静地。

root: 拉丁语 quies（休息）→ quietus（安宁的）→ 古法语 quite → 英语 quiet + -ly → quietly；同族有 quietness、quieten。

sensesIntro.en: The core is little sound; the senses extend to calm behaviour and to action kept out of public view.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「声音小」；义项扩展到举止的平静与避开公众视线的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands turning a door handle very slowly so the latch makes no click.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手极慢地转动门把，让锁舌不发出一声轻响。

branches.en: a latch turned without a sound
a voice lowered in a shared room
branches.cn: 公共房间里压低的声音

branches.en: an apology offered without drama
a new branch opened with no announcement
branches.cn: 没有公告就开张的新分店

branches.en: the same restraint applied to sound and to feeling
branches.cn: 同一种克制，一次用于声音，一次用于情绪

intro.en: The word is the old adjective of rest plus the common adverb ending, so its structure is root, adjective and manner suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示休息的古老形容词加上常见副词词尾，结构为词根、形容词与方式后缀三层。

latinIntro.en: The root reaches English through French, and the adverb adds a native English ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词根经法语进入英语，副词则加上了英语本族的词尾。

definition_zh: 相当；颇；完全；十分；的确
definition_en: to a fairly large degree; completely or entirely; used to agree strongly with what has just been said
core_image: 一杯水被倒到杯口，刚好齐平而不溢出
scene: 看完演出，两人站在剧院门口争论这出戏到底好不好，谁也没有立刻走开。The play was quite good, but the ending felt rushed.
sceneCN: 这里 quite 是「相当、颇」（第 1 个义项：达到较大的程度但未到极致）；句意为这出戏相当不错，只是结尾显得仓促。画面里可留意：剧院门口的灯箱、还没散去的人群。

derivatives.zh: 与 quite 同源的形容词，用于 call it quits，指两清、扯平
同源动词，指停止或离开
re- 加同源词，指回报或报复

senses.title: To a fairly large degree
senses.definition: to a degree that is large but not extreme
senses.definitionCN: 达到较大但并未到极点的程度
senses.example: The film was quite good, though not great.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影相当不错，虽然算不上出色。
senses.why: The oldest sense was completely or free of qualification, and English softened it into a strong but not absolute degree.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「完全、毫无保留」，英语把它弱化为一种强而不绝对的程度。

senses.title: Completely or entirely
senses.definition: entirely, with no reservation, especially in British speech
senses.definitionCN: 完全地、毫无保留地，尤见于英式口语
senses.example: I quite agree with you on that point.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一点上我完全同意你。
senses.why: The word began as a legal term for being clear of a debt or a claim, and being clear of any doubt produced the sense of entirely.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是法律用语，指债务或主张已经清结；既然任何疑问都清除了，就生出「完全」这一层意思。

senses.title: Used to agree strongly
senses.definition: used alone or with a short reply to show strong agreement
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用或作简短回答，表示强烈的同意
senses.example: 'It is cold tonight.' 'Quite.'
senses.exampleCN: 「今晚真冷。」「的确。」
senses.why: If something is quite so, it is entirely so; a bare quite therefore affirms the previous statement without adding anything.
senses.whyCN: 如果某事 quite 如此，就是完全如此；单独一个 quite 因此是在肯定前一句话，不再另加内容。

intro.en: Quite comes from the same Latin root as quiet and quit, through a French word meaning cleared or free; from free of doubt came the sense of completely.
intro.cn: quite 与 quiet、quit 同出一个拉丁词根，经一个意为「清结、自由」的法语词传来；从「无疑」生出了「完全」的意思。

items.en: Quies meant rest, and the related adjective described a person or thing at rest and free from obligation.
items.cn: quies 意为休息，相关形容词形容处于安歇、免于义务的人或物。

items.en: Quietus was used in law for being cleared of a debt or a claim, that is, free and settled.
items.cn: quietus 在法律中用于表示债务或主张已清结，也就是自由、了结。

items.en: Old French quite carried the legal sense of cleared and free, and also the sense of entirely.
items.cn: 古法语 quite 既带有「清结、自由」的法律义，也带有「完全」义。

items.en: Middle English quite meant completely or without reservation, often in phrases of agreement.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quite 意为完全、毫无保留，常用于表示同意的说法。

items.en: Modern English weakened the word in everyday use to a fairly large degree, while keeping the older strong sense in British speech.
items.cn: 现代英语在日常用法中把它弱化为「相当」，而在英式口语里保留了较强的旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same root's English forms; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of degree and agreement.
note.cn: 形近组收同词根的英语形式；近义组收表示程度与同意的副词。

entries.definition: Even in a debt or a dispute, as in call it quits.
entries.definitionCN: 债务或争执两清，如 call it quits。

entries.definition: To a noticeable degree, often with a mild tone.
entries.definitionCN: 达到明显程度地，常带轻微语气。

normalIntro.en: The word began as cleared and free, moved to entirely, and softened to fairly in everyday speech.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「清结、自由」开始，走到「完全」，又在日常口语里弱化为「相当」。

normal.en: Quite, quiet and quit all come from the Latin word for rest; only quite kept the legal sense of settled.
normal.cn: quite、quiet 与 quit 都出自拉丁语「休息」一词，只有 quite 保留了「了结」的法律义。

normal.en: Quite a few means a fairly large number, even though few alone suggests a small one.
normal.cn: quite a few 意为相当多，尽管 few 单独用时表示很少。

normal.en: Not quite is the polite way of saying almost, but not completely.
normal.cn: not quite 是「几乎但不完全」的客气说法。

normal.en: In British speech quite can mean entirely, while in American speech it more often means fairly.
normal.cn: 在英式口语里 quite 可指完全，在美式口语里更常指相当。

normal.en: A single quite in reply means you agree completely with the previous sentence.
normal.cn: 单独一个 quite 作回答，表示你完全同意上一句话。

abstract.en: A word that once meant free of every claim now measures how much of a claim is true.
abstract.cn: 一个曾表示「免除一切主张」的词，如今用来衡量一项主张有多少成真。

abstract.en: Quite is a word of proportion, and proportion is always judged by the ear rather than by the ruler.
abstract.cn: quite 是一个讲分寸的词，而分寸总是由耳朵来判断，而不是由尺子。

abstract.en: The strength of quite depends on the listener, which is why the same sentence can sound like praise or like faint damning.
abstract.cn: quite 的分量取决于听者，所以同一句话既能听起来像称赞，也能像淡淡的贬低。

examples.en: The room is quite small, but it is enough for one person.
examples.cn: 房间相当小，但一个人住够了。

examples.en: Are you quite sure you left the keys here?
examples.cn: 你十分确定把钥匙落在这里了吗？

examples.en: There were quite a few people waiting outside.
examples.cn: 外面等着的人相当多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快特」——比「快」还要特别一点，程度相当高，记住 quite 是相当、完全。

root: 拉丁语 quies（休息）→ quietus（清结、免除）→ 古法语 quite → 英语 quite；同族有 quiet、quit、quits、requite。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being clear and complete; the senses divide into a strong degree, full completeness and bare agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「清结而完整」；义项分为较强程度、完全的完整性，以及单独表示同意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass filled to the brim, level but not spilling.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯水倒到杯口，齐平而不外溢。

branches.en: a film that is better than expected
a debt marked paid in full
a single word of agreement in a quiet room
branches.cn: 安静房间里一个表示同意的单词

branches.en: the same word measuring a degree and closing a discussion
branches.cn: 同一个词既衡量程度，也结束讨论

branches.en: the legal fullness softened into everyday emphasis
branches.cn: 法律的「完全」被软化成日常的强调

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing on the Latin root of rest, and its English relatives are few but old.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「休息」词根上的法语借词，它的英语亲属不多但很古老。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root quiet- also produced quiet and quit, though English split the meanings apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 quiet- 也产生了 quiet 与 quit，只是英语把词义拆开了。

definition_zh: 赛跑；竞赛；种族；急奔；（磨坊）水道
definition_en: a competition to see who is fastest; a contest between people or groups; a group of people sharing ancestry; to move very fast; a channel of water leading to a mill
core_image: 傍晚的跑道上，几名选手同时冲过起跑线
scene: 傍晚的跑道上，发令枪响后几名选手同时冲出起跑线。He won the final race by less than a second.
sceneCN: 这里 race 是「赛跑、竞速比赛」（第 1 个义项：比谁跑得快的比赛）；句意为他以不到一秒的优势赢下了最后一场比赛。画面里可留意：起点线、发令枪、几乎并排的身影。

pos.zh: 赛跑；竞赛；种族；（磨坊）水道
急速行进；参赛；使拼命跑

derivatives.zh: race 加 -er，指参赛者或赛车
race 加 -ing，指赛跑、赛车等竞技活动
race 加 -ial，指与种族有关的
race 加 -ist，指持种族歧视观点的

senses.title: A competition of speed
senses.definition: a contest to find who or what is fastest
senses.definitionCN: 比出谁或什么最快的一种竞赛
senses.example: He won the hundred-metre race.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢下了百米赛跑。
senses.why: The contest sense comes from an old northern word for a rush or a run, so the word began as the movement itself.
senses.whyCN: 比赛义来自一个古老的北方词，意为「急冲、奔跑」，所以这个词最初指的就是那股奔跑。

senses.title: A contest between people or groups
senses.definition: a situation in which people or groups try to be first to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体争相抢先达到某个目标的情形
senses.example: The race for the contract ended in a tie.
senses.exampleCN: 争取这份合同的竞争以平局收场。
senses.why: Once a race was a run toward a line, any struggle to arrive first could be called a race, even without running.
senses.whyCN: 当 race 指朝终点线奔跑之后，任何「抢在前头」的争夺都可以叫 race，即使根本不用跑。

senses.title: A group sharing ancestry
senses.definition: a group of people regarded as sharing ancestry and physical features, a term used with care
senses.definitionCN: 被视为共享血统与外貌特征的一群人，此词使用时须谨慎
senses.example: People of every race took part in the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 各种族的人都参加了这项调查。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source, an Italian word for kind or breed, and its scientific status has been much debated.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同，出自一个意为「种类、品种」的意大利语词，其科学地位一直备受争议。

senses.title: To move very fast
senses.definition: to move at great speed, often in a hurry or in competition
senses.definitionCN: 以很快的速度移动，常带匆忙或竞争意味
senses.example: She raced to catch the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 她飞奔去赶末班车。
senses.why: Since the word first named a rush, the verb simply describes the act of rushing, with or without a contest.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词最初指一股急冲，动词就只是描述急冲这一动作，无论有没有比赛。

senses.title: A channel of water
senses.definition: a fast current of water, especially one made to drive a mill wheel
senses.definitionCN: 流速较快的水道，尤指为驱动磨坊水轮而开的渠道
senses.example: The old mill still stands beside the race.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老磨坊仍然立在水道旁边。
senses.why: Water rushing through a narrow channel moves like a runner, so the old sense of a rush survived in the mill race.
senses.whyCN: 水冲过窄渠时像奔跑者一样急行，于是「急冲」这一古老意思在磨坊水道里保留下来。

intro.en: Race is really two words: the contest sense comes from an old northern word for a rush, while the ancestry sense comes through French and Italian from a word of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: race 实际上是两个词：比赛义来自古老的北方词「急冲」，而种族义经法语与意大利语来自一个来源不确定的词。

items.en: Ras meant a running or a rush, and it entered northern English with the sense of swift movement.
items.cn: ras 意为奔跑、急冲，带着快速运动的意思进入英格兰北部英语。

items.en: Middle English race named a run or a course, and from that a contest of speed.
items.cn: 中古英语的 race 指一次奔跑或一段跑道，由此生出速度竞赛之义。

items.en: A separate French word razza, of uncertain origin, meant a breed or a kind, especially of animals.
items.cn: 另一个来源不确定的法语词 razza 意为品种或种类，尤指动物的品种。

items.en: English applied the breed sense to groups of people, a use that later became scientifically and socially disputed.
items.cn: 英语把「品种」义用到人群上，这一用法后来在科学与社会层面都引发争议。

items.en: Modern English keeps both words: race as a contest and race as a category of people, plus the mill race of flowing water.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两个词：作为竞赛的 race、作为人群类别的 race，以及指流水渠道的磨坊 race。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the word; the near-meaning group gathers words for contests, speed and ancestry.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个词构成的形式；近义组收表示竞赛、速度与血统的词。

entries.definition: A person or vehicle that takes part in races.
The sport of competing for speed.
Connected with a group sharing ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 与共享血统的群体有关的。

entries.definition: Someone who treats people unequally because of their group.
entries.definitionCN: 因所属群体而区别对待他人的人。

entries.definition: A competition in which people try to win.
The activity of trying to do better than others.
To run at top speed for a short distance.
Belonging to a group with shared culture and origin.
entries.definitionCN: 属于共享文化与来源的群体。

normalIntro.en: The contest sense grew from a word for a rush of movement, and the ancestry sense grew from a word for breed; English keeps both under one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 比赛义从表示「急冲」的词生长出来，种族义从表示「品种」的词生长出来；英语把两者放在同一个拼写之下。

normal.en: Race as a contest and race as a category of people have different origins that happen to share one spelling.
normal.cn: 作为竞赛的 race 与作为人群类别的 race 来源不同，只是碰巧共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: A race against time is a race with no competitor but the clock.
normal.cn: race against time 是没有对手、只与时钟赛跑的比赛。

normal.en: Racer, racing and racial all come from the same short word with different endings.
normal.cn: racer、racing、racial 都是同一个短词加上不同词尾。

normal.en: A mill race is water rushing through a channel, which shows how old the sense of a rush really is.
normal.cn: mill race 指冲过渠道的水，可见「急冲」这一古老意思有多深。

normal.en: The human race uses race in the broad sense of all people together, not in the sense of a category.
normal.cn: the human race 用的是「全人类」这一宽泛义，而不是「某一类别」义。

abstract.en: Sorting people into races says more about the sorter than about the people being sorted.
abstract.cn: 把人分成种族，更多说明分类者本身，而不是被分类的人。

abstract.en: A race is exciting because everyone agrees on the same finish line, which is also why disagreements about the line are so bitter.
abstract.cn: 比赛令人兴奋，因为大家认同同一条终点线，这也正是关于终点线的分歧如此激烈的原因。

abstract.en: Speed is easy to measure and easy to admire, which is why so much of modern life is arranged as a race.
abstract.cn: 速度容易测量，也容易赞美，所以现代生活有很大一部分被安排成一场比赛。

examples.en: She came second in the school race.
examples.cn: 她在学校赛跑中得了第二。

examples.en: The two companies are in a race to launch first.
examples.cn: 两家公司在争抢谁先发布。

examples.en: He raced down the stairs when he heard the alarm.
examples.cn: 听到警报，他飞奔下楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐丝」——像一根锐利的丝线划过终点，速度极快，记住 race 是赛跑、竞赛。

root: 比赛义源于古诺斯语 ras（奔跑、急冲）；种族义经法语与意大利语来自 razza（品种，来源不确定）；两词在英语中同形。同族有 racer、racing、racial。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rush; one branch runs from rush to contest, the other from breed to ancestry, and a third survives in the channel of a mill.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「急冲」；一条支线从急冲走到竞赛，另一条从品种走到血统，还有一条留在磨坊的水道里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: runners leaving the start line together on an evening track.
core.cn: 核心意象：傍晚跑道上同时冲出起跑线的选手。

branches.en: a gun fired beside a track
two firms chasing one contract
branches.cn: 两家公司争抢同一份合同

branches.en: a form asking for ancestry
feet taking the stairs three at a time
the same rush, once on legs and once in a mill channel
branches.cn: 同一种急冲，一次靠双腿，一次在磨坊渠道里

intro.en: The contest word is native and northern, the ancestry word came through French and Italian, and English adds its usual endings to both.
intro.cn: 表示竞赛的词是本族词，来自北方；表示血统的词经法语和意大利语传来；英语给两者加上了惯用的词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for either word.
latinIntro.cn: 这两个来源都没有可靠的拉丁语出处记录。

definition_zh: 收音机；广播；无线电；用无线电发送
definition_en: a device that receives broadcast sound; the broadcasting of sound by radio waves; the technology of sending signals by electromagnetic waves; to send a message by radio
core_image: 一台老式收音机的指针停在刻度盘上，扬声器微微发亮
scene: 厨房里，老式收音机的指针在刻度上滑动，水壶的蒸汽把窗玻璃蒙上一层白雾。She turned the radio down when the phone rang.
sceneCN: 这里 radio 是「收音机」（第 1 个义项：接收广播声音的装置）；句意为电话响时她把收音机的声音调小了。画面里可留意：刻度盘上的指针、冒汽的水壶、蒙雾的窗。

pos.zh: 用无线电发送；用无线电联络

derivatives.zh: radio 与 man 复合，指从事无线电通信工作的人
radio 与 controlled 复合，指靠无线电操纵的
radio- 与 isotope 复合，指具有放射性的同位素

senses.title: A receiving device
senses.definition: a piece of equipment that picks up broadcast sound and plays it
senses.definitionCN: 接收广播声音并播放出来的设备
senses.example: She turned on the radio in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她在厨房里打开了收音机。
senses.why: The device is named by shortening the technical word for wireless communication, so the machine carries the name of the method.
senses.whyCN: 这台设备的名字是「无线通信」这一技术词的缩略，因此机器承袭了方法的名字。

senses.title: Broadcasting by radio waves
senses.definition: the activity or service of sending sound to many listeners at once
senses.definitionCN: 把声音同时发送给许多听众的活动或服务
senses.example: The interview will be on the radio tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 这段采访今晚会在广播里播出。
senses.why: Once sound could travel without wires, broadcasting became a public service, and English called it simply the radio.
senses.whyCN: 声音既能不用电线传播，广播便成了公共服务，英语就径直称之为 the radio。

senses.title: Wireless communication technology
senses.definition: the technology of sending signals through space by electromagnetic waves
senses.definitionCN: 通过电磁波在空间中发送信号的技术
senses.example: The message was sent by radio from the ship.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息是用船上的无线电发出的。
senses.why: This is the broadest sense: the physical method itself, used by ships, aircraft and stations alike.
senses.whyCN: 这是最宽泛的一层：指这种物理方法本身，船只、飞机与电台都在使用。

senses.title: To send a message by radio
senses.definition: to communicate with someone by radio, especially in an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 用无线电与某人联络，尤指在紧急情况下
senses.example: The pilot radioed for help as the fog closed in.
senses.exampleCN: 雾合拢上来时，飞行员用无线电求救。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, naming the act of sending a message through the same technology.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，指通过同一技术发送消息这一动作。

intro.en: Radio is a shortened form of words built on the Latin word for ray; the technology of wireless signalling took the name of the rays it uses.
intro.cn: radio 是建立在拉丁语表示射线的词之上的词语的缩略；无线通信技术采用了它所使用的那种射线的名字。

items.en: Radius meant a spoke or a ray, a straight line sent out from a centre.
items.cn: radius 指辐条或射线，即从中心射出的一条直线。

items.en: Radiare meant to send out rays, and the stem radi- entered scientific language as a combining form.
items.cn: radiare 意为发出射线，词干 radi- 作为构词成分进入科学语言。

items.en: Early wireless signalling was called radiotelegraphy, sending telegraph messages by electromagnetic waves.
items.cn: 早期的无线通信被称为 radiotelegraphy，即用电磁波发送电报。

items.en: English speakers shortened the long technical word to radio in the early twentieth century.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，英语使用者把这个冗长的技术词缩略为 radio。

items.en: Modern English uses radio for the device, the broadcast service, the technology and the act of signalling.
items.cn: 现代英语用 radio 指设备、广播服务、技术以及发送信号的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of rays; the near-meaning group gathers words for broadcasting and wireless signalling.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「射线」词干上的词；近义组收表示广播与无线通信的词。

entries.definition: A detection system using reflected radio waves.
entries.definitionCN: 利用反射无线电波进行探测的系统。

entries.definition: A line from the centre of a circle to its edge.
entries.definitionCN: 从圆心到圆周的一条线。

entries.definition: Energy sent out as waves or particles.
entries.definitionCN: 以波或粒子形式发出的能量。

entries.definition: A person who works with radio equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 从事无线电设备工作的人。

entries.definition: To send sound or pictures to many receivers.
entries.definitionCN: 把声音或图像发送给许多接收者。
不通过连接导线工作的。

entries.definition: A device that picks up transmitted signals.
entries.definitionCN: 接收所传送信号的装置。

entries.definition: The sending out of signals or power.

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin ray in modern dress: wireless signalling was named after the rays that carry it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是穿上现代外衣的拉丁语「射线」：无线通信以承载它的射线命名。

normal.en: Radio, radius and radiation all begin with the Latin word for a ray leaving a centre.
normal.cn: radio、radius 与 radiation 都从拉丁语表示「从中心射出的射线」一词开始。

normal.en: On the radio names the service, while a radio names the box on the kitchen table.
normal.cn: on the radio 指广播服务，而 a radio 指厨房桌上的那台机器。

normal.en: Radio silence means no signals are being sent, often by a ship or an aircraft that must stay unheard.
normal.cn: radio silence 指不发送任何信号，常是船只或飞机必须保持静默时。

normal.en: To radio someone is to send a message by radio rather than by phone.
normal.cn: to radio 某人就是用无线电而不是电话发送消息。

normal.en: Radar is radio detection and ranging, a child of the same technology.
normal.cn: radar 是无线电探测与测距，是同一技术的产物。

abstract.en: Radio made a voice present in millions of rooms at once, the first everyday experience of shared listening.
abstract.cn: 广播让一个声音同时出现在千万个房间里，这是人们第一次日常体验到共同收听。

abstract.en: A device named after invisible rays taught people to trust what they could hear but not see.
abstract.cn: 一台以看不见的射线命名的机器，教会人们去相信听得到却看不见的东西。

abstract.en: Radio silence is powerful because absence of signal is also a message.
abstract.cn: 无线电静默之所以有力，是因为没有信号本身也是一种消息。

examples.en: The radio on the shelf still works after forty years.
examples.cn: 架子上那台收音机用了四十年还能工作。

examples.en: Her talk will be broadcast on the radio this evening.
examples.cn: 她的谈话今晚将在广播中播出。

examples.en: The coast guard radioed the fishing boat to warn it of the storm.
examples.cn: 海岸警卫队用无线电通知渔船有暴风雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞迪欧」——声音不用电线，像射线一样飘进屋里，记住 radio 是收音机、无线电。

root: 拉丁语 radius（射线、辐条）→ radiare（发出射线）→ 科学构词成分 radi- → radiotelegraphy → 缩略为英语 radio；同族有 radar、radiation、radius。

sensesIntro.en: The core is signalling by rays; the senses divide into the receiving device, the broadcast service, the technology and the act of sending a message.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「靠射线传信」；义项分为接收设备、广播服务、技术本身，以及发送消息的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old radio's needle resting on a dial, its speaker faintly warm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台老式收音机的指针停在刻度盘上，扬声器微微发热。

branches.en: a dial turned by a thumb
a voice filling a kitchen
an aerial on a ship's roof
a message sent through fog
branches.cn: 穿过雾发出去的一条消息

branches.en: the same signal, once as a machine and once as a programme
branches.cn: 同一个信号，一次是机器，一次是节目

intro.en: The word is a modern shortening of a scientific compound built on the Latin stem for ray, with English endings for people and instruments.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在拉丁语「射线」词干上的科学复合词的现代缩略，加上表示人与器械的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem radi- is shared with radius and radiation, and it still builds new technical words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 radi- 与 radius、radiation 共用，至今仍在构成新的技术词。

definition_zh: 铁路（英式）；铁路系统；铁路运输
definition_en: a track of rails with stations and signals, the usual British word for a railroad; the organization and system that runs trains; transport by train
core_image: 山谷里一座长满草旧车站，月台尽头立着褪色站牌
scene: 山谷里的旧车站已经长满草，月台尽头还立着一块褪色的站牌。The old railway once carried timber down the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 railway 是「铁路（英式说法）」（第 1 个义项：带车站与信号系统的轨道线路）；句意为这条旧铁路曾把木料运下山谷。画面里可留意：长草的月台、褪色站牌、通向谷底的轨线。

pos.zh: 铁路（英式）；铁路系统；铁路运输

derivatives.zh: railway 的第一成分，指单根轨条
美式对应词，指铁路或铁路公司
railway 与 man 复合，指铁路员工

senses.title: A track with stations and signals
senses.definition: a line of rails with its stations, signals and equipment, the usual British word for a railroad
senses.definitionCN: 带车站、信号与设备的轨道线路，英式英语对铁路的常用说法
senses.example: The old railway closed in the nineteen sixties.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧铁路在二十世纪六十年代停运了。
senses.why: British English joined rail and way to name the whole line, while American English chose rail and road.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把 rail 与 way 组合起来命名整条线路，而美式英语选择了 rail 与 road。

senses.title: The organization and system
senses.definition: the body that owns the line and runs the trains
senses.definitionCN: 拥有线路并经营列车的机构
senses.example: She works for the national railway.
senses.exampleCN: 她在国家铁路部门工作。
senses.why: As with many networks, the physical line and the institution that operates it are called by one name.
senses.whyCN: 和许多网络一样，实体线路与运营它的机构共用一个名字。

senses.title: Transport by train
senses.definition: the carrying of people or goods by train, considered as a mode of transport
senses.definitionCN: 以火车运送人或货物，作为一种运输方式
senses.example: Goods moved by railway until the road was widened.
senses.exampleCN: 在公路拓宽之前，货物靠铁路运输。
senses.why: The system's name also names the service it provides, which is why people speak of sending something by railway.
senses.whyCN: 系统的名字也指它提供的服务，所以人们会说用铁路运送某物。

intro.en: Railway is a nineteenth-century English compound of rail and way, coined in Britain to name the new lines of track.
intro.cn: railway 是十九世纪的英语复合词，由 rail 与 way 组成，在英国被造出来命名新兴的轨道线路。

items.en: Rail came from the Latin word for a straight rule through French, and named the metal bar itself.
items.cn: rail 经法语来自拉丁语表示直尺的词，指的就是那根金属条。

items.en: Way is a native English word for a path or a route, older than any railway.
items.cn: way 是英语本族词，指路径或路线，比任何铁路都古老。

items.en: The compound railway named the way made of rails, a route built for locomotives.
items.cn: 复合词 railway 指由轨条铺成的路，为机车修建的路线。

items.en: British English kept railway for the line and the system, while American English settled on railroad.
items.cn: 英式英语保留 railway 指线路与系统，美式英语则固定用 railroad。

items.en: Modern English uses railway for the track, the company and the transport service, especially outside North America.
items.cn: 现代英语用 railway 指轨道、公司与运输服务，尤其在北美以外。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same compound; the near-meaning group gathers words for rail systems and routes.
note.cn: 形近组收同一复合词的形式；近义组收表示铁路系统与路线的词。

entries.definition: The American word for the same system.
A single metal bar for wheels.
entries.definitionCN: 供车轮行驶的一根金属条。

entries.definition: A person employed by a railway.
A single route of track between places.
entries.definitionCN: 两地之间的一条轨道线路。

entries.definition: A route of track or wire between places.
entries.definitionCN: 两地之间的轨道或线路。

entries.definition: The pair of rails a train runs on.
entries.definitionCN: 火车行驶其上的那对钢轨。

entries.definition: The carrying of people or goods.

normalIntro.en: The word is rail plus way, the British way of naming a road of rails; the American cousin is railroad.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 rail 加 way，是英式命名「轨条之路」的方式；它的美国亲戚是 railroad。

normal.en: Railway is rail plus way, railroad is rail plus road: two languages, one idea.
normal.cn: railway 是 rail 加 way，railroad 是 rail 加 road：两种语言，同一个想法。

normal.en: A railway station is where the line meets the town, and a railway carriage is one coach on it.
normal.cn: railway station 是线路与城镇相接之处，railway carriage 是线上的一节车厢。

normal.en: The national railway is the publicly owned system, as opposed to a private company.
normal.cn: the national railway 指公有的铁路系统，与私营公司相对。

normal.en: By railway is less common than by rail, which is the usual short phrase.
normal.cn: by railway 不如 by rail 常用，后者才是通常的简短说法。

normal.en: A railwayman works on the line, a word that survives mainly in British writing.
normal.cn: railwayman 指在铁路上工作的人，这个词主要保留在英式书面语里。

abstract.en: A railway is a promise that the same route will be there tomorrow, which is why it changed how people planned their lives.
abstract.cn: 铁路是一种承诺：同一条路线明天仍在那里，因此它改变了人们安排生活的方式。

abstract.en: Cutting a railway through a valley is an act that both connects and divides the land.
abstract.cn: 在山谷里修一条铁路，既连接也分割了这片土地。

abstract.en: When a railway closes, the towns along it quietly become places people pass by instead of stop at.
abstract.cn: 一条铁路停运后，沿线的城镇悄然变成人们经过而不再停留的地方。

examples.en: The railway between the two towns was built in eighteen fifty.
examples.cn: 两镇之间的铁路建于1850年。

examples.en: He found work on the railway after the mill closed.
examples.cn: 磨坊关闭后，他在铁路部门找到了工作。

examples.en: Timber was carried by railway until the road was improved.
examples.cn: 在公路改善之前，木料靠铁路运输。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「锐欧威」——轨条铺成一条路，向远方延伸，记住 railway 是铁路。

root: rail（轨条，源自拉丁语 regula）+ way（路，英语本族词）复合而成，十九世纪出现；同族有 railroad、railwayman。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a way of rails; the senses divide into the British railway line, the system that runs it, and transport by train.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「由轨条铺成的路」；义项分为英式铁路线路、运营它的系统，以及铁路运输。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an overgrown station in a valley, a faded sign at the platform's end.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷里长满草的旧车站，月台尽头一块褪色的站牌。

branches.en: a track disappearing into a valley
a timetable in a station office
branches.cn: 车站办公室里的时刻表

branches.en: timber stacked on a flat wagon
rails rusting under long grass
the same line, once busy and once abandoned
branches.cn: 同一条线路，一次繁忙，一次废弃

intro.en: The compound joins a Latin-derived rail to a native way, and English endings extend it to workers and to individual lines.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把源自拉丁语的 rail 与本族的 way 结合，英语词尾又把它扩展到工作者与单条线路。

latinIntro.en: Only rail has a Latin source, the word for a straight rule.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 rail 有拉丁语来源，即表示直尺的词。

items.meaning: a stopping place on a line

definition_zh: 雨；雨水；下雨；如雨般落下
definition_en: water that falls from clouds in drops; to fall as rain; a large number of things falling or arriving at once
core_image: 屋檐下连成一线落下的水珠
scene: 早晨的街道上，行人撑起伞，水沿着屋檐一线线落下。The rain kept the whole village indoors for two days.
sceneCN: 这里 rain 是「雨」（第 1 个义项：从云中落下的水滴）；句意为这场雨让整个村子两天都待在室内。画面里可留意：伞面、屋檐滴落的水线、空荡的街道。

derivatives.zh: rain 加 -y，指多雨的、下雨的
rain 与 fall 复合，指一段时间内的降雨量
rain 与 coat 复合，指防雨的外套

senses.title: Water falling from clouds
senses.definition: water that falls from clouds in drops and reaches the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从云中以水滴形式落下并到达地面的水
senses.example: The rain lasted all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这场雨下了一整个上午。
senses.why: Old English regn named the falling water directly, and the word has stayed close to the weather ever since.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 regn 直接命名这种落下的水，此后这个词一直紧贴天气这一含义。

senses.title: To fall as rain
senses.definition: to fall from the sky as drops of water, used of the weather itself
senses.definitionCN: 以水滴形式从天空落下，用于描述天气本身
senses.example: It rained for three days without stopping.
senses.exampleCN: 雨连下了三天没停。
senses.why: The noun became an impersonal verb, so English can say it rains without naming who or what is acting.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了无人称动词，因此英语可以说 it rains，而不必指出动作的执行者。

senses.title: A great number falling at once
senses.definition: a large number of things coming down or arriving together, as if falling like drops
senses.definitionCN: 大量事物像水滴一样同时落下或到来
senses.example: A rain of stones fell from the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵石块从崖上落下。
senses.why: Because rain is countless drops arriving together, the word became a picture for anything that comes in a shower.
senses.whyCN: 雨是无数水滴一同到来，因此这个词成了任何「成阵而至」之物的画面。

intro.en: Rain is a native English word from Old English regn, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: rain 是英语本族词，来自古英语 regn，在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Regn meant rain, and it was used in compounds for storms and wet weather.
items.cn: regn 意为雨，也用于构成表示风暴与潮湿天气的复合词。

items.en: The word is reconstructed in older Germanic with the same sense, and related forms appear across northern Europe.
items.cn: 这个词在更早的日耳曼语中被重构为同样的意思，相关形式遍布北欧。

items.en: Middle English rain kept the spelling close to the old form while the verb rained developed beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语的 rain 拼写接近古形，同时发展出动词 rained。

items.en: Rain combined with fall and coat to name what rain does and what protects against it.
items.cn: rain 与 fall、coat 组合，命名雨的作用以及防雨之物。

items.en: Modern English uses rain for the water, the weather, and figuratively for anything arriving in quantity.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rain 指水、天气，并比喻任何大量到来之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and one homophone; the near-meaning group gathers words for falling water.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词与一个同音词；近义组收表示落水的词。

entries.definition: The amount of rain that falls in a period.
A coat that keeps rain out.
The period during which a monarch rules, a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 君主统治的时期，同音但不同源。

entries.definition: A very heavy fall of rain.
Light rain falling in fine drops.
entries.definitionCN: 以细小雨滴落下的毛毛雨。

entries.definition: Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow or hail.
entries.definitionCN: 以雨、雪或冰雹形式从云中落下的水。

normalIntro.en: The word names the falling water, then the weather, then anything that arrives like drops in a shower.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词先命名落下的水，再指天气，最后指任何像水滴一样成阵而至的东西。

normal.en: Rain and reign sound the same, but one falls from the sky while the other is held by a monarch.
normal.cn: rain 与 reign 同音，但一个从天上落下，一个由君主掌握。

normal.en: Rainy is the adjective, rainfall is the measured amount, and raincoat is the thing you wear.
normal.cn: rainy 是形容词，rainfall 是测得的雨量，raincoat 是穿在身上的东西。

normal.en: It rained is impersonal: the it does not point to anyone, because weather has no actor.
normal.cn: it rained 是无人称句：it 不指向任何人，因为天气没有执行者。

normal.en: Rain or shine is the phrase for doing something whatever the weather.
normal.cn: rain or shine 是无论天气如何都要做某事的说法。

normal.en: A rain of stones uses the weather word for anything falling in great numbers.
normal.cn: a rain of stones 用天气词指大量落下的任何东西。

abstract.en: Rain is the most ordinary proof that something can arrive without being invited.
abstract.cn: 雨是「事物会不请自来」这件事最平常的证明。

abstract.en: Farmers read rain as promise or threat, which shows how one word can carry both hope and fear.
abstract.cn: 农民把雨读成许诺或威胁，可见同一个词能同时承载希望与恐惧。

abstract.en: A rain of stones and a rain of questions share the word because both overwhelm by number.
abstract.cn: 石雨与问题雨共用一个词，因为两者都以数量压倒了人。

examples.en: The rain stopped just before the match began.
examples.cn: 比赛开始前雨刚好停了。

examples.en: It rained so hard that the road disappeared under water.
examples.cn: 雨下得太大，路面被水淹没了。

examples.en: A rain of small stones rattled on the roof.
examples.cn: 一阵小石块噼里啪啦打在屋顶上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞恩」——天上落下的水滴一颗颗，记住 rain 是雨、下雨。

root: 古英语 regn（雨）→ 中古英语 rain → 现代英语 rain；同族有 rainy、rainfall、raincoat。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is falling water; the senses divide into the water itself, the weather, and anything arriving in a shower.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「落下的水」；义项分为水本身、天气，以及任何成阵而至之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: drops falling in a continuous line from the edge of a roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：水珠从屋檐边连成一线落下。

branches.en: an empty street under umbrellas
a window grey with weather
stones rattling down a cliff
the same falling, once as water and once as stones
branches.cn: 同一种下落，一次是水，一次是石头

branches.en: weather that arrives and things that arrive in numbers
branches.cn: 到来的天气与成批到来的东西

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its family is built from English compounds and a simple adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是本族短词，其词族由英语复合词与一个简单的形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 举起；提高；筹集；抚养；提出；引起
definition_en: to lift something to a higher position; to increase an amount or level; to collect money for a purpose; to bring up children or animals; to put a subject forward for discussion; to cause a feeling or reaction
core_image: 一只举到半空的手，掌心朝前
scene: 会议室里，一位成员把手举到半空，示意想就预算发问。She raised her hand and waited for the chair to notice her.
sceneCN: 这里 raise 是「举起」（第 1 个义项：把某物抬到更高的位置）；句意为她举起手，等主席注意到她。画面里可留意：举到半空的手、朝前的手掌、会议桌。

pos.zh: 举起；提高；筹集；抚养；提出；引起

derivatives.zh: raise 加 -er，指筹集者或饲养者
raise 加 -ing，指举起、抚养或筹集的过程
fund 与 raiser 复合，指筹款活动或筹款人

senses.title: To lift to a higher position
senses.definition: to move something upward to a higher place or level
senses.definitionCN: 把某物向上移到更高的位置或水平
senses.example: Raise your hand if you have a question.
senses.exampleCN: 有问题请举手。
senses.why: The word came into English from Old Norse with the plain sense of setting something upright or lifting it, and that physical act is still the centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古诺斯语进入英语，本义是把某物立起或抬起，这个身体动作至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To increase an amount
senses.definition: to make a price, level or amount higher
senses.definitionCN: 使价格、水平或数量变高
senses.example: The shop raised its prices twice this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店今年两次提价。
senses.why: Raising a thing higher and raising a number higher use the same image, so the word moved easily from objects to quantities.
senses.whyCN: 把东西举高与把数字提高用的是同一幅画面，所以这个词从实物轻易地转向了数量。

senses.title: To collect money
senses.definition: to gather money or support for a purpose, often for charity
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的募集钱款或支持，常指慈善
senses.example: The class raised money for the animal shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 全班为动物收容所筹集了钱款。
senses.why: Money that is brought together and lifted into a common fund looks like something raised up from many hands.
senses.whyCN: 把分散的钱聚拢并抬进一个共同基金，看起来就像从许多只手中把东西举起来。

senses.title: To bring up children or animals
senses.definition: to care for a child or an animal until it is grown
senses.definitionCN: 照料孩子或动物直到长大
senses.example: She raised three children on her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她独自抚养了三个孩子。
senses.why: To raise a child is to lift that person up through years of care, and the same verb serves for animals on a farm.
senses.whyCN: 抚养孩子就是通过多年照料把人「托举」起来，同一个动词也用于农场里的动物。

senses.title: To put a subject forward
senses.definition: to bring a question or subject to other people's attention for discussion
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或话题提到别人面前供讨论
senses.example: He raised a question about the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 他就日程安排提了一个问题。
senses.why: A subject brought into a conversation is lifted into view, so the word of lifting also means to mention for discussion.
senses.whyCN: 被带进对话的话题被举到众人眼前，于是「举起」这个词也指提出来讨论。

senses.title: To cause a feeling or reaction
senses.definition: to produce a feeling, doubt or reaction in people
senses.definitionCN: 在人们心中产生某种感受、疑虑或反应
senses.example: The news raised fears of another delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这则消息引起了对再次延误的担忧。
senses.why: If an action lifts a feeling into notice, it causes that feeling, and this sense extends the word from things to emotions.
senses.whyCN: 一个举动把某种情绪举到众人注意之中，就是引起了那种情绪，这一义项把词从实物扩展到情感。

intro.en: Raise came into English from Old Norse, where the verb meant to set something upright; it is related to rise but carries an object.
intro.cn: raise 从古诺斯语进入英语，那个动词意为把某物立起；它与 rise 相关，但必须带宾语。

items.en: Reisa meant to raise or to set upright, and Norse settlers brought it into northern English.
items.cn: reisa 意为举起或立起，诺斯定居者把它带入英格兰北部。

items.en: Raise and rise come from the same family, but rise is what a thing does and raise is what someone does to it.
items.cn: raise 与 rise 同属一族，但 rise 是事物自身发生的动作，raise 是某人对它施加的动作。

items.en: Middle English raise kept the sense of lifting and setting up, and added the sense of bringing up a child.
items.cn: 中古英语的 raise 保留了举起与竖立的意思，并增加了抚养孩子的义项。

items.en: From lifting objects came lifting prices, collecting money, raising a subject and raising a feeling.
items.cn: 从举物生出提价、筹钱、提出话题与引起情绪等义。

items.en: Modern English uses raise for lifting, increasing, collecting, nurturing, mentioning and causing, and as a noun for a pay increase.
items.cn: 现代英语用 raise 表示举起、增加、筹集、养育、提及与引起，并作名词指加薪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of lifting and increasing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根上的形式；近义组收表示举起与增加的动词。

entries.definition: To go upward by itself, without an object.
entries.definitionCN: 自身向上移动，不带宾语。

entries.definition: To begin to exist, especially of a problem.
A person or thing that raises.
The act of lifting, collecting or bringing up.
entries.definitionCN: 举起、筹集或抚养的行为。

entries.definition: To move something upward with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地把某物向上移动。

entries.definition: To make or become larger in amount.
To gather things or money together.
To care for someone while they grow.
entries.definitionCN: 在某人成长过程中给予照料。

normalIntro.en: The word always needs an object: someone raises something, whether a hand, a price, money, a child, a question or a fear.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词总要带宾语：某人把某样东西举起，无论是手、价格、钱款、孩子、问题还是恐惧。

normal.en: Raise needs an object and rise does not: you raise your hand, but the sun rises.
normal.cn: raise 需要宾语而 rise 不需要：你举起手，而太阳自己升起。

normal.en: A pay raise in American English is what British English calls a pay rise.
normal.cn: 美式英语的 a pay raise 就是英式英语的 a pay rise。

normal.en: Raise money means collect it, while raise prices means increase them: the same verb, two directions of lift.
normal.cn: raise money 是筹集，raise prices 是提高：同一个动词，两种「抬升」方向。

normal.en: Raise children and raise animals both mean care for them until grown.
normal.cn: raise children 与 raise animals 都指照料其长大。

normal.en: Raise a question is to bring it up, not to answer it.
normal.cn: raise a question 是把问题提出来，而不是回答它。

abstract.en: Almost everything people do to improve a situation can be said with this one verb, which is why it appears so often in meetings.
abstract.cn: 人们为改善处境所做的几乎每件事都能用这一个动词表达，所以它在会议里出现得如此频繁。

abstract.en: To raise a child is to lift someone you cannot fully control, and that is the daily risk of parenting.
abstract.cn: 抚养孩子就是托举一个你无法完全掌控的人，这正是养育的日常风险。

abstract.en: A question raised is a question someone must now carry, even if nobody answers it.
abstract.cn: 一个被提出的问题，就成了某人必须背负的问题，即使没有人回答。

examples.en: He raised the box above his head and held it there.
examples.cn: 他把箱子举过头顶，稳稳停在那里。

examples.en: The government plans to raise the minimum wage next year.
examples.cn: 政府计划明年提高最低工资。

examples.en: They raised enough money to rebuild the bridge.
examples.cn: 他们筹到了足够的钱重建那座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞兹」——把东西锐利地向上托起，记住 raise 是举起、提高。

root: 古诺斯语 reisa（举起、立起）→ 中古英语 raise → 现代英语 raise；与 rise、arise 同族。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an upward lift; the senses divide into lifting an object, raising a number, collecting money, bringing up the young, putting a subject forward and causing a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「向上托举」；义项分为举起实物、提高数字、筹集钱款、养育幼小、提出话题与引起情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifted into the air, palm forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举到半空、掌心朝前的手。

branches.en: a box held above the head
a price tag rewritten higher
branches.cn: 被改写成更高数字的价签

branches.en: coins gathered from many hands
branches.cn: 从许多只手里聚拢的硬币

branches.en: a child guided step by step
the same lift applied to a question and to a fear
branches.cn: 同一种抬升，一次用于问题，一次用于恐惧

intro.en: The word is a Norse borrowing, and English built its relatives with an agent suffix and a participle rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是古诺斯语借词，英语用施动者词尾与分词来构成亲属词，而非拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语同族词记录。

definition_zh: 等级；地位；军衔；行列；把…分等级；位居
definition_en: a position on a scale of importance or quality; an official grade, especially in the armed forces; a row of people or things; to place people or things in order; to hold a particular position
core_image: 一排士兵按高矮站成的笔直队列
scene: 操场上，士兵们按个头从高到矮站成一条直线，队伍整齐得像尺子画出来。The captain held the rank of major for many years.
sceneCN: 这里 rank 是「军衔」（第 2 个义项：军队中的正式等级）；句意为这位上尉多年保持少校军衔。画面里可留意：整齐的队伍、按身高排成的直线、军装的肩章。

derivatives.zh: rank 加 -ing，指名次、排名
rank 加 -ed，指被排定名次的
out- 与 rank 复合，指地位高于
high 与 ranking 复合，指级别高的

senses.title: A position on a scale
senses.definition: a position on a scale of importance, quality or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 在重要性、质量或成就的尺度上所居的位置
senses.example: She reached the top rank of her profession.
senses.exampleCN: 她达到了本行业的最高等级。
senses.why: A row of soldiers fixes each person in a place, and that fixed place became a measure of standing.
senses.whyCN: 一排士兵把每个人固定在某个位置，这个固定位置便成了地位的衡量。

senses.title: An official grade
senses.definition: an official grade held by a member of the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 武装部队成员所持的正式等级
senses.example: The captain held the rank of major.
senses.exampleCN: 这位上尉持有少校军衔。
senses.why: Armies number their rows from bottom to top, so the place a soldier occupies became his official grade.
senses.whyCN: 军队把队列自下而上编号，因此士兵所占的位置便成了他的正式等级。

senses.title: A row of people or things
senses.definition: a row of people or things placed side by side
senses.definitionCN: 并排而立的一排人或物
senses.example: The chairs stood in a neat rank along the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子沿墙排成整齐的一行。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a row, the line in which people or objects are drawn up.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是一排，即人或物被排成的直线。

senses.title: To place in order
senses.definition: to arrange people or things in order according to quality or importance
senses.definitionCN: 按质量或重要性把人或物排成次序
senses.example: The judges ranked the entries from best to worst.
senses.exampleCN: 评委把参赛作品从优到劣排出名次。
senses.why: If a rank is a row, to rank is to put things into that row in their proper places.
senses.whyCN: 既然 rank 是一行，to rank 就是把事物各归其位地排进那一行。

senses.title: To hold a position
senses.definition: to have a particular position in a scale, list or group
senses.definitionCN: 在尺度、名单或群体中占据特定位置
senses.example: The university ranks among the best in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学位居全国最好的大学之列。
senses.why: From the act of placing came the state of being placed, so a thing can rank, that is, stand somewhere in the order.
senses.whyCN: 从「摆放」的动作生出「被摆放」的状态，因此某物可以 rank，即在次序中站于某处。

intro.en: Rank comes from Old French ranc, a row, probably from the same Frankish source as range; a row of soldiers became a scale of official grades.
intro.cn: rank 来自古法语 ranc（一行），可能与 range 同出法兰克语；一排士兵后来变成了等级阶梯。

items.en: Old French ranc meant a row or line, especially a row of soldiers.
items.cn: 古法语 ranc 意为一行或一列，尤指一排士兵。

items.en: The word is traced to a Frankish term for a circle or band of men, the same source as range.
items.cn: 这个词可追溯到法兰克语中表示一圈或一队人的词，与 range 同源。

items.en: Middle English rank kept both the row and the military line, and added the idea of a grade.
items.cn: 中古英语 rank 既保留「一排」与军阵的线，又加上了等级的意思。

items.en: Because a formation places each soldier in a fixed spot, rank came to mean a soldier's official grade.
items.cn: 由于队列把每个士兵放在固定位置，rank 便引申为士兵的正式等级。

items.en: Modern English ranks people and things by quality, and uses the verb to rank for placing and for holding a place.
items.cn: 现代英语按质量给人或物排等级，并用动词 rank 表示排位和位居。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers row words and close forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for grade and standing.
note.cn: 形近组收表示行列的词与近形词；近义组收表示等级与地位的词。

entries.definition: A row or extent, the close cousin of rank.
entries.definitionCN: 一行或范围，rank 的近亲。

entries.definition: A position on a list of results.
A person who patrols a wild area.
A level of quality or rank.
A person's social or official standing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的社会地位或官方身份。

entries.definition: A place in a scale or order.
entries.definitionCN: 在尺度或次序中的位置。

entries.definition: A division based on quality or rank.
entries.definitionCN: 按质量或等级划分的类别。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a row of bodies, then becomes the place each body occupies, and finally the act and state of standing somewhere in an order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一排身体开始，变成每具身体所占的位置，最后成为「处于某个次序位置」的动作与状态。

normal.en: Rank and range come from the same old word for a row.
normal.cn: rank 与 range 同出表示「一行」的那个古词。

normal.en: A rank of soldiers is a row; an officer's rank is his place in that row.
normal.cn: 士兵的 rank 是一排；军官的 rank 是他在这一排里的位置。

normal.en: To rank first is to stand at the head of the row.
normal.cn: to rank first 就是站在这支队伍的最前头。

normal.en: Rank and file names the ordinary soldiers who stand in the rows.
normal.cn: rank and file 指站在队列里的普通士兵。

normal.en: To rank something is to put it into its proper place in the line.
normal.cn: 给某物 rank 就是把它放到队列中合适的位置。

abstract.en: Rank measures where you stand, not who you are.
abstract.cn: rank 衡量的是你站在哪里，而不是你是谁。

abstract.en: A list ranks names the way a formation ranks bodies, by a fixed order.
abstract.cn: 名单给名字排名，正如队列给身体排名，都依一种固定次序。

abstract.en: To outrank someone is to stand one step nearer the front.
abstract.cn: outrank 某人，就是比他站得离排头更近一步。

examples.en: He rose to the rank of colonel.
examples.cn: 他升到了上校军衔。

examples.en: The university ranks among the best in the country.
examples.cn: 这所大学位居全国最好的大学之列。

examples.en: The students were ranked by their test scores.
examples.cn: 学生们按考试成绩被排了名次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「队伍排成一排」——rank 本是一行士兵，后来引申为等级与军衔。

root: 古法语 ranc（一行）→ 中古英语 rank → 现代英语 rank；与 range 同源，可能出自法兰克语「一圈人」。同族有 ranking、ranked、outrank。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a row of bodies; the senses move from a grade of standing to a military grade, to the row itself, and then to the act and state of ordering.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一排身体；义项从地位等级，到军衔，再到行列本身，最后到排序的动作与状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soldiers standing shoulder to shoulder in a straight line, each at a fixed spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：士兵肩并肩站成一条直线，每人各占一个固定位置。

chain: A FIXED SPOT IN THE ROW

branches.en: soldiers standing shoulder to shoulder
steps of a ladder from low to high
stripes on a uniform sleeve
cards sorted by number
a name near the top of a list
branches.cn: 名单接近顶端的一个名字

intro.en: The word is a borrowing from Old French, and its family is built with English suffixes, a prefix and fixed phrases.
intro.cn: 这个词借自古法语，其词族由英语后缀、一个前缀与固定短语构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word; the older root is Frankish.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录；更早的词根是法兰克语。

definition_zh: 迅速的；急剧的；急流
definition_en: moving or happening very quickly; happening suddenly and to a great degree; a part of a river where the water flows fast and rough over rocks
core_image: 河水在乱石间奔涌成一道白色的急流
scene: 山谷里的河水撞上乱石，翻起白色的浪头，一路奔涌而下。The river's rapid current swept the boat downstream in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 rapid 是「迅速的」（第 1 个义项：移动或发生得极快）；句意为河中湍急的水流几秒钟就把小船冲向下游。画面里可留意：翻白的浪头、乱石、被冲走的小船。

derivatives.zh: rapid 加 -ly，指迅速地
rapid 加 -ity，指迅速、快捷
rapid 加 -s，指河中湍急的一段
rapid 加 -ness，指迅速的状态

senses.title: Moving very quickly
senses.definition: moving or happening at great speed
senses.definitionCN: 以极快的速度移动或发生
senses.example: The country has seen rapid economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家经历了迅速的经济增长。
senses.why: Latin rapidus described anything carried along swiftly, and the word kept that plain sense of speed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rapidus 形容任何被迅速带走之物，这个词保留了这层朴素的「快」。

senses.title: Sudden and great in degree
senses.definition: happening suddenly and to a large degree, used especially of change
senses.definitionCN: 突然发生且幅度很大，尤用于变化
senses.example: A rapid change in the weather caught the climbers off guard.
senses.exampleCN: 天气的急剧变化让登山者措手不及。
senses.why: Something carried away fast can also change fast, so rapid extended from speed of motion to speed of change.
senses.whyCN: 被迅速带走之物也会迅速改变，于是 rapid 从运动之快扩展到变化之快。

senses.title: Fast rough water
senses.definition: a stretch of river where the water runs fast and breaks over rocks
senses.definitionCN: 河水中流得很快、在岩石上翻涌的一段
senses.example: The raft bounced through the rapids.
senses.exampleCN: 木筏在急流中颠簸而过。
senses.why: The same image of water seized and carried along named the place in a river where the current runs hardest.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「水被卷走」的意象，命名了河中水流最猛的那一段。

intro.en: Rapid goes back to Latin rapere, to seize and carry away; what is rapid is literally carried along at speed.
intro.cn: rapid 可追溯到拉丁语 rapere（抓住并带走）；被 rapid 形容之物，字面上就是被迅速卷走的。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off, and it pictured force dragging something away.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住并带走，画面是力量把某物拖走。

items.en: Rapidus described anything carried along swiftly, from a rushing river to a fast flight.
items.cn: rapidus 形容任何被迅速带走之物，从奔腾的河到飞快的飞行。

items.en: Old French took the Latin word as rapide and kept the sense of great speed.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词借作 rapide，保留了「极快」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rapid applied the word to motion, to events, and to rivers that run fast.
items.cn: 中古英语 rapid 把这个词用于运动、事件，以及流得快的河。

items.en: Modern English uses rapid for quick motion and quick change, and the plural rapids for rough, fast water.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rapid 指快速运动与快速变化，用复数 rapids 指湍急的水流。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and one word from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers ordinary words for speed.
note.cn: 形近组收同根的形式与一个同源词；近义组收表示速度的常用词。

entries.definition: A stretch of fast, rough river water.
The act of seizing property by force, from the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力夺取财物，同一拉丁词根。

entries.definition: Moving or happening at high speed.
Moving or done in a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 在短时间内移动或完成的。
移动极快，常含顺畅之意。

normalIntro.en: The word pictures things seized and carried along; from that force come the senses of fast motion, fast change and fast water.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的画面是被抓住并卷走的东西；从这股力量生出快速运动、快速变化与湍急水流三层意思。

normal.en: Rapid and rapere share the image of something seized and carried off at speed.
normal.cn: rapid 与 rapere 共享「某物被抓住并迅速卷走」的画面。

normal.en: Rapids are the parts of a river where the water itself runs fast.
normal.cn: rapids 就是河中水本身流得最快的地方。

normal.en: Rapid growth and rapid change both describe movement in time, not in space.
normal.cn: rapid growth 与 rapid change 描述的都是时间中的移动，而不是空间中的移动。

normal.en: Rapid is stronger than quick: it suggests real force behind the speed.
normal.cn: rapid 比 quick 更强，暗含速度背后有一股真实的力量。

normal.en: The same root gives rapine, the taking of goods by force.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 rapine，即用武力夺取财物。

abstract.en: Speed that carries things away is the oldest sense of rapid.
abstract.cn: 「把东西卷走的快」是 rapid 最古老的意思。

abstract.en: We call change rapid when it moves faster than we can follow.
abstract.cn: 当变化快过我们跟上的速度，我们才称它 rapid。

abstract.en: A rapid is water in a hurry, and that is the word's whole picture.
abstract.cn: 急流是匆匆赶路的水，这就是这个词的全部画面。

examples.en: The country has seen rapid economic growth.
examples.cn: 这个国家经历了迅速的经济增长。

examples.en: A rapid change in the weather caught the climbers off guard.
examples.cn: 天气的急剧变化让登山者措手不及。

examples.en: The raft bounced through the rapids.
examples.cn: 木筏在急流中颠簸而过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「拉皮的」——被人拽着飞快拖走，记住 rapid 是迅速的。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（抓住带走）→ rapidus（被迅速带走的）→ 古法语 rapide → 现代英语 rapid；同族有 rapidly、rapidity、rapids。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being seized and carried along; the senses divide into fast motion, fast change, and fast rough water.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被抓住并卷走」；义项分为快速运动、快速变化与湍急的水流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current of white water tearing through rocks and dragging everything with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股白色的水流撕开乱石，把一切都拖走。

branches.en: a sprinter leaving the blocks
a price line climbing steeply
white water breaking over rocks
speed in motion and speed in change
a fast runner and a fast river
branches.cn: 飞快的奔跑者与湍急的河流

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built with English suffixes and compounds on the same root.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由同一词根上的英语后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the word its root: rapere, to seize, and rapidus, carried swiftly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给了这个词词根：rapere（抓住）与 rapidus（被迅速带走）。

definition_zh: 迅速地；急剧地；接连不断地
definition_en: at great speed; within a short time and to a great degree; one after another in quick succession
core_image: 秒针绕着表盘飞速转圈
scene: 仪表盘上的指针一格接一格地跳动，数字不断向上翻。Prices rose rapidly during the shortage.
sceneCN: 这里 rapidly 是「迅速地」（第 1 个义项：以极快的速度）；句意为短缺期间物价迅速上涨。画面里可留意：跳动的指针、不断上翻的数字。

pos.zh: 迅速地；急剧地；接连不断地

derivatives.zh: rapidly 去掉 -ly，指迅速的
rapid 加 -ity，指迅速、快捷
rapid 加 -s，指河中湍急的一段
rapid 加 -ness，指迅速的状态

senses.title: At great speed
senses.definition: at great speed, of movement or action
senses.definitionCN: 移动或行动以极快的速度
senses.example: Prices rose rapidly during the shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 短缺期间物价迅速上涨。
senses.why: Rapidly is rapid plus the adverb ending, so it describes an action done with the speed that rapid names.
senses.whyCN: rapidly 是 rapid 加副词词尾，因此它描述以 rapid 所指的那种速度完成的动作。

senses.title: Sharply in a short time
senses.definition: suddenly and to a great degree within a short time
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内突然而大幅度地
senses.example: The situation changed rapidly after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告发布后局势急剧变化。
senses.why: Because rapid also means sudden in degree, the adverb can describe change that is sharp as well as fast.
senses.whyCN: 由于 rapid 也指幅度上的突然，这个副词既能描述快，也能描述变得剧烈。

senses.title: One after another
senses.definition: in quick succession, with little pause between events
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个，事件之间几乎没有停顿
senses.example: Reports came rapidly, one after another.
senses.exampleCN: 报告接连不断地传来。
senses.why: When things follow at great speed, the adverb marks not one fast act but a stream of them in quick succession.
senses.whyCN: 当事物以极快速度接连而来，这个副词标记的不是一个快动作，而是一连串紧接的动作。

intro.en: Rapidly is rapid with the English adverb ending -ly, and rapid itself goes back to Latin rapere, to seize and carry away.
intro.cn: rapidly 是 rapid 加上英语副词词尾 -ly，而 rapid 本身可追溯到拉丁语 rapere（抓住并带走）。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off, the picture behind all forms of this family.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住并带走，是整个词族背后的画面。

items.en: Rapidus described what is carried along swiftly, and English borrowed it as rapid.
items.cn: rapidus 形容被迅速带走之物，英语把它借作 rapid。

items.en: English kept rapid as an adjective of speed before any adverb was formed from it.
items.cn: 英语先把 rapid 作为表示速度的形容词保留下来，之后才由它构成副词。

items.en: The old English ending -lice became -ly, which turns an adjective into an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -lice 演变为 -ly，把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Modern English uses rapidly for speed, for sharp change, and for events that follow in quick succession.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rapidly 表示速度、急剧变化，以及紧接而来的事件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base word and its close forms; the near-meaning group gathers common adverbs of speed.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的原形与近形；近义组收常用的速度副词。

entries.definition: Fast, rough water in a river.

normalIntro.en: The adverb adds manner to the adjective rapid, so it tells how fast an action is done, how sharp a change is, or how closely events follow.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词给形容词 rapid 加上「方式」，说明动作做得多快、变化多剧烈，或事件跟得多紧。

normal.en: Rapidly is simply rapid with the adverb ending -ly.
normal.cn: rapidly 就是 rapid 加上副词词尾 -ly。

normal.en: Rapidly and quickly both mean at speed, but rapidly sounds more formal and more forceful.
normal.cn: rapidly 与 quickly 都表示快速，但 rapidly 更正式、更有力。

normal.en: Prices that rise rapidly climb a long way in a short time.
normal.cn: rise rapidly 的物价在短时间内涨了很多。

normal.en: Events that follow rapidly come one after another without pause.
normal.cn: follow rapidly 的事件一个接一个，没有停顿。

normal.en: The root rapere, to seize, is still visible in the force of rapidly.
normal.cn: 词根 rapere（抓住）在 rapidly 的力量感里仍然看得见。

abstract.en: Rapidly measures not distance but the rate at which time is filled.
abstract.cn: rapidly 衡量的不是距离，而是时间被填满的速率。

abstract.en: What happens rapidly often outruns our ability to react.
abstract.cn: 发生得 rapidly 的事，常常快过我们反应的能力。

abstract.en: To change rapidly is to move faster than the old shape can hold.
abstract.cn: 变化 rapidly，就是动得比旧形态所能容纳的更快。

examples.en: The situation changed rapidly after the announcement.
examples.cn: 公告发布后局势迅速变化。

examples.en: The disease spread rapidly through the crowded camp.
examples.cn: 疾病在拥挤的营地中迅速传播。

examples.en: Reports came rapidly, one after another.
examples.cn: 报告接连不断地传来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「表针飞转」——指针一圈圈飞快地转，记住 rapidly 是迅速地。

root: 拉丁语 rapere → rapidus → 英语 rapid + 副词后缀 -ly → rapidly；同族有 rapid、rapidity、rapids。

sensesIntro.en: The core is speed in action; the senses divide into plain speed, sharp change in a short time, and events following one another closely.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是动作中的速度；义项分为单纯的速度、短时间内的急剧变化，以及紧接而来的事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock hand spinning round the dial, faster than the eye can follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟表指针绕表盘飞转，快得眼睛跟不上。

branches.en: a clock hand spinning fast
a steeply rising graph
a row of lights flashing in turn
speed and suddenness together
branches.cn: 速度与突然性合在一起

branches.en: sharp change repeated again and again

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with two English layers, the adjective rapid and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加两层英语成分：形容词 rapid 与副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the root: rapere, to seize, and rapidus, carried swiftly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给出词根：rapere（抓住）与 rapidus（被迅速带走）。

definition_zh: 宁愿；相当；更确切地说
definition_en: more willingly, used in would rather; to a certain degree, fairly; more precisely, used to correct or contrast
core_image: 分岔的小路上脚步偏向更安静的一侧
scene: 路口分出两条小道，脚步不自觉地偏向更安静的那一条。I would rather walk than take the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 rather 用于 would rather，是「宁愿」（第 1 个义项：更愿意做某事）；句意为比起坐公交，我更愿意走路。画面里可留意：分岔的小路、偏向一侧的脚步。

derivatives.zh: rather 加 -ish，指有点儿、稍微
同源的古词，指早的、迅速的

senses.title: More willingly
senses.definition: more willingly, used with would to express a preference
senses.definitionCN: 更愿意，与 would 连用表达偏好
senses.example: I would rather walk than take the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 比起坐公交，我更愿意走路。
senses.why: Old English hraþor meant sooner, and what one chooses sooner is what one prefers, so the word became a marker of preference.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hraþor 意为更早，而人更早选择的正是更偏爱的，于是这个词成了偏好的标记。

senses.title: To a certain degree
senses.definition: to a moderate degree, more than a little but less than very
senses.definitionCN: 达到中等程度，多于一点而少于「很」
senses.example: The film was rather good.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片相当不错。
senses.why: From the sense of more, the word weakened into a plain marker of degree, meaning fairly or quite.
senses.whyCN: 从「更多」的意思出发，这个词弱化为单纯的程度标记，意为「相当」或「颇」。

senses.title: More precisely
senses.definition: used to correct or sharpen what has just been said, or to introduce a better word
senses.definitionCN: 用于更正或精确化刚说过的话，或引出更恰当的说法
senses.example: He is not a teacher, but rather a writer.
senses.exampleCN: 他不是教师，而是作家。
senses.why: When one word is replaced by a better one, the speaker is choosing the preferable term, and rather marks that correction.
senses.whyCN: 当一个词被更恰当的词替换时，说话人正是在选更可取的说法，rather 标记这一更正。

intro.en: Rather is a native English word, the old comparative of an adjective meaning quick or prompt; the idea of sooner grew into the idea of preference.
intro.cn: rather 是英语本族词，原是意为「迅速、敏捷」的形容词的比较级；「更早」的观念长成了「更愿意」。

items.en: Hrathor was the comparative of hræþ, quick or prompt, and meant sooner or more readily.
items.cn: hraþor 是 hræþ（迅速、敏捷）的比较级，意为更早或更乐意。

items.en: Because what one does sooner is what one prefers, the word took on the sense of more willingly.
items.cn: 因为人更早去做的，正是更愿意做的，这个词便带上「更乐意」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rather kept both the older sense of sooner and the newer sense of preference.
items.cn: 中古英语 rather 既保留较早的「更早」，也保留较新的「更愿意」。

items.en: From the idea of more, rather weakened into a word for a moderate degree, meaning fairly.
items.cn: 从「更多」的观念出发，rather 弱化为表示中等程度的词，即「相当」。

items.en: Modern English uses rather in would rather for choice, for moderate degree, and to correct or sharpen a statement.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rather 于 would rather 表选择，表中等程度，以及用来更正或精确化说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers two words often confused with rather and two fixed phrases; the near-meaning group gathers degree words and a word of preference.
note.cn: 形近组收两个易与 rather 混淆的词与两个固定短语；近义组收程度词与一个表偏好的词。

entries.definition: A small rodent, a different word.
A measure or a speed, a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 一种比率或速度，另一词。

entries.definition: Instead of, used to set one choice against another.
entries.definitionCN: 而不是，用来把一种选择与另一种对照。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as sooner, becomes more willingly, then a moderate degree, then a correction of words.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「更早」开始，变成「更愿意」，再变成中等程度，最后成为对说法的更正。

normal.en: Rather and rat look alike, but a rat is an animal and rather is a choice or a degree.
normal.cn: rather 与 rat 形近，但 rat 是动物，rather 是选择或程度。

normal.en: Would rather is the phrase for saying what you would prefer.
normal.cn: would rather 是用来说自己更愿意做什么的短语。

normal.en: Rather than sets one choice against another, as in walk rather than drive.
normal.cn: rather than 把一种选择与另一种对照，如 walk rather than drive。

normal.en: Rather good means good to a fair degree, not very good.
normal.cn: rather good 指相当好，而不是非常好。

normal.en: Or rather introduces a better word for what was just said.
normal.cn: or rather 引出对刚说过的话更恰当的说法。

abstract.en: Preference is measured by what you would choose sooner.
abstract.cn: 偏好可以用「你更早选择什么」来衡量。

abstract.en: Rather softens a judgment, leaving room for doubt or modesty.
abstract.cn: rather 让判断变柔，为疑虑或谦逊留出余地。

abstract.en: To correct with rather is to admit that the first word was not quite right.
abstract.cn: 用 rather 更正，就是承认第一个词还不够准确。

examples.en: I would rather stay at home tonight.
examples.cn: 今晚我宁愿待在家里。

examples.en: The film was rather good.
examples.cn: 这部影片相当不错。

examples.en: He is not a teacher, but rather a writer.
examples.cn: 他不是教师，而是作家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「岔路口偏一步」——两条路摆着，脚步偏向更愿意走的那条，记住 rather 是宁愿、相当。

root: 古英语 hræþ（迅速）→ 比较级 hraþor（更早、更乐意）→ 中古英语 rather → 现代英语 rather；同族有 rathe。没有可靠的拉丁语来源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a comparison of readiness; the senses move from preference to moderate degree to a correction of wording.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「乐意程度的比较」；义项从宁愿，到中等程度，再到对措辞的更正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fork in a path where the foot leans toward the quieter way.
core.cn: 核心意象：路边出现岔口，脚步偏向更安静的那条路。

branches.en: a foot turning toward one path
branches.cn: 脚步转向其中一条小路

branches.en: a mark halfway up a scale
branches.cn: 刻度尺上居中偏上的标记

branches.en: a word crossed out and replaced
branches.cn: 一个被划掉并替换的词

branches.en: leaning toward a choice and leaning toward a degree
branches.cn: 偏向一种选择，也偏向一个程度

branches.en: softening a claim and correcting a word

intro.en: The word is native and short, and its small family is built from an old comparative ending and fixed phrases.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且为本族词，其不大的词族由古老的比较级词尾与固定短语构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded; the word is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录；这个词是日耳曼语本族词。

definition_zh: 到达；伸手够到；达到；与…联系；可及范围
definition_en: to arrive at a place; to stretch out a hand to touch something; to attain a level or amount; to get in touch with someone; the distance within which something can be reached
core_image: 手臂伸向高架上的一只杯子
scene: 高架上的杯子有点远，手臂伸到极限才碰到杯沿。She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
sceneCN: 这里 reach 是「伸手够到」（第 2 个义项：把手伸出去触到某物）；句意为她用指尖够到了顶层架子。画面里可留意：伸出的手臂、高架上的杯子、碰到的指尖。

pos.zh: 到达；伸手够到；达到；与…联系

derivatives.zh: reach 加 -able，指可到达的、可联系的
out 与 reach 复合，指主动外联、延伸服务
over- 与 reach 复合，指做得过头、超越能力

senses.title: To arrive at a place
senses.definition: to arrive at a place, especially after effort or a journey
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地，尤指经过努力或一段行程之后
senses.example: We reached the village before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在天黑前到达了村子。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to stretch out to a point, and arriving is stretching your journey until it touches the destination.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「伸到一点」，而抵达就是让行程一直伸到触着目的地。

senses.title: To stretch out and touch
senses.definition: to put out a hand or arm in order to touch or take something
senses.definitionCN: 伸出手或手臂去触到或拿取某物
senses.example: She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
senses.exampleCN: 她用指尖够到了顶层架子。
senses.why: The word first pictured a hand extended until it met an object, and this literal picture is still the core.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘的是手一直伸到与物体相接，这一字面画面至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To attain a level
senses.definition: to arrive at a particular level, amount or standard after a process
senses.definitionCN: 经过一个过程达到某一水平、数量或标准
senses.example: Sales reached a record high last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月的销售额达到了历史新高。
senses.why: If a hand can reach a height, then a process can reach a level, so the word extended from space to measure.
senses.whyCN: 手能伸到一个高度，一个过程也能达到一个水平，于是这个词从空间扩展到度量。

senses.title: To get in touch
senses.definition: to succeed in speaking or writing to someone
senses.definitionCN: 成功地与某人通话或通信
senses.example: I tried to reach him by phone all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我一上午都在试着打电话联系他。
senses.why: Making contact is like stretching across a distance until the other person is touched, so reach came to mean communicate with.
senses.whyCN: 建立联系就像跨越距离一直伸到触着对方，于是 reach 引申为「与……沟通」。

senses.title: The distance one can reach
senses.definition: the distance or range within which something can be reached or used
senses.definitionCN: 某物能被触及或使用所及的距离或范围
senses.example: The cookies are within the child's reach.
senses.exampleCN: 饼干在孩子够得着的范围内。
senses.why: From the act of stretching came the noun for how far that stretch goes, hence the range one can cover.
senses.whyCN: 从「伸展」的动作生出名词，表示这一伸能到多远，因此就是可覆盖的范围。

intro.en: Reach is a native English word from Old English ræcan, to stretch out or extend, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: reach 是英语本族词，来自古英语 ræcan（伸出、延伸），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Ræcan meant to stretch out or extend toward something, often a hand toward an object.
items.cn: ræcan 意为向某物伸出或延伸，常指手伸向物体。

items.en: Related Germanic verbs carry the same picture of extending toward a point.
items.cn: 相关的日耳曼语动词带有同样的「朝一点延伸」的画面。

items.en: Middle English reach widened from the hand to the journey, so one could reach a town as well as a shelf.
items.cn: 中古英语 reach 从手扩展到行程，因此既能 reach 一个架子，也能 reach 一座城镇。

items.en: As the word moved from space to levels and to people, it took in reaching a figure and reaching a person.
items.cn: 随着这个词从空间转到水平与人，它纳入了达到某个数字与联系到某个人。

items.en: Modern English uses reach for arriving, stretching, attaining, contacting, and for the range so covered.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reach 表示抵达、伸手、达到、联系，以及由此覆盖的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and fixed phrases; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of arriving, attaining and contacting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与固定短语；近义组收表示抵达、达到与联系的动词。

entries.definition: To extend a hand or make contact.
To stretch a hand toward something.
To go too far or attempt too much.
To reach a level or goal after effort.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力达到某一水平或目标。

entries.definition: To extend a limb or a thing.
